text: Two small transformers watch a flow through one sensor. Both predict the next reading well.
say: Two small transformers watch a flow through one sensor. Both predict the next reading well.
heard: Two small transformers watch a flow through one sensor. Both predict the next reading well.

text: Now ask each to rebuild the whole field of one velocity component from what it learned.
say: Now ask each to rebuild the whole field of one velocity component from what it learned.
heard: Now ask each to rebuild the whole field of one velocity component from what it learned.

text: One gets it nearly right. The other is about seventy times worse.
say: One gets it nearly right. The other is about seventy times worse.
heard: One gets it nearly right. The other is about 70 times worse.

text: Both forecast the next step well, but they are very different on the inside.
say: Both forecast the next step well, but they are very different on the inside.
heard: Both forecast the next step well, but they are very different on the inside.

text: Today's paper: A Mechanistic Analysis of Transformers for Dynamical Systems.
say: Today's paper: A Mechanistic Analysis of Transformers for Dynamical Systems.
heard: Today's paper, A Mechanistic Analysis of Transformers for Dynamical Systems.

text: The model sees one number per time step, from one sensor.
say: The model sees one number per time step, from one sensor.
heard: The model sees one number per time step from one sensor.

text: It takes the last five readings as tokens.
say: It takes the last five readings as tokens.
heard: It takes the last five readings as tokens.

text: Then attention mixes them into a short vector, the latent state: its internal guess of where the system is.
say: Then attention mixes them into a short vector, the latent state: its internal guess of where the system is.
heard: Then attention mixes them into a short vector, the latent state, its internal guess of where the system is.

text: A small network predicts the next reading from it.
say: A small network predicts the next reading from it.
heard: A small network predicts the next reading from it.

text: The vector's length is the model's room. Two numbers, or three.
say: The vector's length is the model's room. Two numbers, or three.
heard: The vector's length is the model's room, two numbers or three.

text: Delay embedding theory says five readings are enough for a state on a two-dimensional surface: two times two, plus one.
say: Delay embedding theory says five readings are enough for a state on a two-dimensional surface: two times two, plus one.
heard: Delay embedding theory says five readings are enough for a state on a two-dimensional surface. Two times two plus one.

text: First test: a reaction-diffusion equation, known as the Chafee-Infante equation.
say: First test: a reaction-diffusion equation, known as the Chafee Infante equation.
heard: First test, a reaction diffusion equation known as the Chaffee-Infante equation.

text: Picture a rod, pinned at zero at both ends. Its shape changes, then settles.
say: Picture a rod, pinned at zero at both ends. Its shape changes, then settles.
heard: Picture a rod pinned at zero at both ends. Its shape changes, then settles.

text: In the long run, its shapes lie on a two-dimensional surface, built from a few sine waves.
say: In the long run, its shapes lie on a two-dimensional surface, built from a few sine waves.
heard: In the long run, its shapes lie on a two-dimensional surface, built from a few sine waves.

text: The model gets one sensor, near the left end. Five readings: in principle, enough information.
say: The model gets one sensor, near the left end. Five readings: in principle, enough information.
heard: The model gets one sensor near the left end, five readings, in principle enough information.

text: But that surface is symmetric about zero: here is our simulation of it, with its two mirror halves.
say: But that surface is symmetric about zero: here is our simulation of it, with its two mirror halves.
heard: But that surface is symmetric about zero. Here is our simulation of it, with its two mirror halves.

text: Now view it through the sensor, two readings at a time.
say: Now view it through the sensor, two readings at a time.
heard: Now view it through the sensor, two readings at a time.

text: The wide surface is squeezed into a thin needle. States that were far apart nearly touch.
say: The wide surface is squeezed into a thin needle. States that were far apart nearly touch.
heard: The wide surface is squeezed into a thin needle, states that were far apart nearly touch.

text: In principle, the information is still in the five readings. The model just has to pull it apart.
say: In principle, the information is still in the five readings. The model just has to pull it apart.
heard: In principle, the information is still in the five readings. The model just has to pull it apart.

text: How much room does that take?
say: How much room does that take?
heard: How much room does that take?

text: With a latent of two numbers, the model squashes the surface into a thick curve.
say: With a latent of two numbers, the model squashes the surface into a thick curve.
heard: With a latent of two numbers, the model squashes the surface into a thick curve.

text: Across ten seeds it is unstable: some runs do worse than a network with no attention.
say: Across ten seeds it is unstable: some runs do worse than a network with no attention.
heard: Across ten seeds, it is unstable. Some runs do worse than a network with no attention.

text: Give it a third number, and the surface unfolds. The sine-wave amplitudes can be read off the latent.
say: Give it a third number, and the surface unfolds. The sine-wave amplitudes can be read off the latent.
heard: Give it a third number, and the surface unfolds. The sine wave amplitudes can be read off the latent.

text: The authors' reading: the extra room lets attention unfold first. Then the network projects back down to two.
say: The authors' reading: the extra room lets attention unfold first. Then the network projects back down to two.
heard: The author's reading. The extra room lets attention unfold first. Then the network projects back down to two.

text: Second test: flow past a cylinder, shedding a trail of vortices.
say: Second test: flow past a cylinder, shedding a trail of vortices.
heard: Second test, flow past a cylinder, shedding a trail of vortices.

text: The Reynolds number sets the regime, from one hundred to seven hundred fifty: one run each.
say: The Reynolds number sets the regime, from one hundred to seven hundred fifty: one run each.
heard: The Reynolds number sets the regime from 100 to 750, one run each.

text: Again, one sensor, a latent of three numbers, and five to seven readings.
say: Again, one sensor, a latent of three numbers, and five to seven readings.
heard: Again, one sensor, a latent of three numbers and five to seven readings.

text: Testing adds six values inside the training range, and three just outside it.
say: Testing adds six values inside the training range, and three just outside it.
heard: Testing adds six values inside the training range and three just outside it.

text: First, the model is not told the Reynolds number.
say: First, the model is not told the Reynolds number.
heard: first the model is not told the reynolds number

text: Its latent loops for different runs overlap. Nearby points can mean different regimes.
say: Its latent loops for different runs overlap. Nearby points can mean different regimes.
heard: Its latent loops for different runs overlap. Nearby points can mean different regimes.

text: One-step errors are lowest mid-range, and grow toward the edges, most of all for held-out runs.
say: One-step errors are lowest mid-range, and grow toward the edges, most of all for held-out runs.
heard: One-step errors are lowest mid-range and grow toward the edges, most of all for held-out runs.

text: Give it the Reynolds number as an input, and the loops separate, in order. Errors drop and even out.
say: Give it the Reynolds number as an input, and the loops separate, in order. Errors drop and even out.
heard: Give it the Reynolds number as an input and the loops separate in order. Errors drop and even out.

text: Then a harder test. From the latent alone, rebuild the whole field of one velocity component.
say: Then a harder test. From the latent alone, rebuild the whole field of one velocity component.
heard: Then a harder test. From the latent alone, rebuild the whole field of one velocity component.

text: With the Reynolds number, the mean absolute error is about one ten-thousandth.
say: With the Reynolds number, the mean absolute error is about one ten-thousandth.
heard: With the Reynolds number, the mean absolute error is about one ten thousandth.

text: Without it, about seventy times worse, and fifty times worse in the wake, where shedding is most sensitive.
say: Without it, about seventy times worse, and fifty times worse in the wake, where shedding is most sensitive.
heard: Without it, about 70 times worse, and 50 times worse in the wake, where shedding is most sensitive.

text: In the first test, the readings held enough information in principle, but the latent had too little room.
say: In the first test, the readings held enough information in principle, but the latent had too little room.
heard: In the first test, the readings held enough information in principle, but the latent had too little room.

text: In the second, there was room, but a hidden parameter got folded in.
say: In the second, there was room, but a hidden parameter got folded in.
heard: In the second, there was room, but a hidden parameter got folded in.

text: Same lesson: one-step accuracy is not latent identifiability. Each true state needs its own place inside.
say: Same lesson: one-step accuracy is not latent identifiability. Each true state needs its own place inside.
heard: Same lesson. One-step accuracy is not latent identifiability. Each true state needs its own place inside.

text: Now, our extrapolation. This part comes from us, not from the paper.
say: Now, our extrapolation. This part comes from us, not from the paper.
heard: Now our extrapolation. This part comes from us, not from the paper.

text: Climate emulators, like ACE and SamudrACE, learn to step a whole climate state forward.
say: Climate emulators, like ACE and Samudrace, learn to step a whole climate state forward.
heard: Climate emulators, like ACE and Samadrace, learn to step a whole climate state forward.

text: Forcing, like carbon dioxide, plays the Reynolds number’s role. Leave it out, and different climates can blur together inside.
say: Forcing, like carbon dioxide, plays the Reynolds number’s role. Leave it out, and different climates can blur together inside.
heard: Forcing, like carbon dioxide, plays the Reynolds numbers role. Leave it out, and different climates can blur together inside.

text: Some of the state may be hidden, like the deep ocean for an atmosphere-only emulator, or deep soil moisture, so the current state alone may not be enough.
say: Some of the state may be hidden, like the deep ocean for an atmosphere-only emulator, or deep soil moisture, so the current state alone may not be enough.
heard: Some of the state may be hidden, like the deep ocean for an atmosphere-only emulator, or deep soil moisture. So the current state alone may not be enough.

text: A good one-step score is not enough: test spectra and long-run statistics too.
say: A good one-step score is not enough: test spectra and long-run statistics too.
heard: A good one-step score is not enough. Test spectra and long-run statistics, too.

text: Two questions to bring to journal club.
say: Two questions to bring to journal club.
heard: Two questions to bring to Journal Club.

text: If two models predict the next step equally well, what test would show which one has the sounder inside?
say: If two models predict the next step equally well, what test would show which one has the sounder inside?
heard: If two models predict the next step equally well, what test would show which one has the sounder inside?

text: And in a climate emulator, what plays the missing Reynolds number? How would we notice?
say: And in a climate emulator, what plays the missing Reynolds number? How would we notice?
heard: And in a climate emulator, what plays the missing Reynolds number? How would we notice?

text: The takeaway: enough information is not enough. A model needs room to unfold it, and the parameters that tell regimes apart.
say: The takeaway: enough information is not enough. A model needs room to unfold it, and the parameters that tell regimes apart.

text: See you at journal club.
